findings.title: A deferred urgent request is assigned to a disconnected physical worker and permanently stops recovery mode.
findings.description: The corrected same-worker queue retains old reports, but the urgent loop checks only whether their sid is busy. In general.debug=false recovery mode, disconnect removes the physical worker and its current urgent assignment while leaving its completed deferred reports retained. When another worker finishes its valid urgent response, the urgent loop removes the next retained report and issues a new assignment to the removed sid. Its emit has no recipient. The session validator correctly refuses a report from that unregistered sid, so this assignment can never complete. No active transfer timer exists, and the periodic task does not advance simulated-time rounds.
findings.reachability: Two physical workers with max_concurrency=2 on one device, per_round=4, minimum_clients=1, asynchronous simulated wall time, request_update=true, staleness_bound=1, rounds=10 and general.debug=false. Actual selection/batching/ingress creates round-1 reports 7/2/8/9, followed by 9 in rounds 2 and 3. Logical clients 7 and 8 belong to the same reused physical worker. The default staleness predicate issues client 7 to lost and client 2 to survivor, deferring client 8. Disconnect lost, then finish survivor/client 2 through real handlers. The server issues client 8 to the absent lost session.

reproduction.observed: Only survivor remains registered. assignments={lost:8}, training_sids=[lost], training_clients=[8], update_requested[8]=true, active_transfers=[], close_called=0; round and round_after_periodic both equal 3. Absent-session response is rejected before parsing. Final failure is the intended no-dead-session-assignment assertion after cleanup.
reproduction.stubs: Outbound emit is AsyncMock. _send generates inert reports/payloads via actual ingress. Aggregation, wrap_up and close are inert; selection, batching, queue construction, default urgency predicate, assignment validation, disconnect recovery branch, second urgent completion and periodic task are production code. No trainer snapshot decoder is invoked.

findings.required_correction: Handle retained/deferred urgency when its physical worker disappears. Never create an outstanding assignment for an unregistered sid. Continue or end with a bounded surfaced failure according to the existing disconnect policy, keeping usable completed reports and exact byte accounting consistent. Add this actual-batching degradation regression and verify surviving-worker progress or explicit termination. Preserve current session rejection and concurrent requests for live distinct workers; no auth, nonce or wire change is needed.
findings.test_gap: The new shared-worker correction regression finishes both responses from a live worker. The disconnect regression clears one active transfer but has no deferred urgent report and does not test subsequent round progress.
findings.baseline_boundary: This is a remaining material failure in the in-scope correction and recovery path, not a claim that general.debug=false recovery first became defective in this commit. Initial R2B-03 already prevented the normal same-worker flow; correcting its serialization exposes the deferred-worker-loss case.

R2B-03.status: Responsive-worker acceptance passes; recovery corner remains blocked by R2B-04
R2B-03.result: Actual single-worker rounds 7/2/9 then 9/9 issue exactly one outstanding urgent assignment, preserve the other report/payload and 190-byte ownership until dispatch, accept both responses, reject wrong/deferred/old/unknown identities, aggregate both and reach round 4. Distinct-worker assignments are established before any emit await; immediate response inside each emit passes without premature aggregation.

R2B-01.result: Selective removal restores the heap. Actual ingress-created partial heap selects [20,9,28] and [20,9,28,31], with the independently recorded finish-time reference. Simulated wall time stays at 50 for earlier responses in both minimum-selection and stale-drain paths.

R2B-02.result: Two distinct retained completions for logical ID 7 across workers each count once at the actual _select_clients send-await boundary. 190+190 bytes against budget 400 reject the third 169-byte report before load_pickle. Reuse releases only its cache; malformed third-worker ingress and first-worker disconnect preserve queued bytes. Processed release and close clear the correct owners and queue objects. Legacy report/payload values remain visible.

R2B-L01.result: The cumulative reserve check enforces max_buffered_bytes as well as max_payload_bytes before append. Actual client socket and local HTTP S3 reject 82-byte payloads at a 20-byte cap and clear transfer state; bounded simulated-file cap remains consistent.
